newsitem.title: GERMANY: German president says concerned about Nazi victims.
newsitem.headline: German president says concerned about Nazi victims.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog met Jewish leaders on Monday and discussed the issues of compensation for eastern European Holocaust survivors and of former war criminals who are receiving state pensions.
A World Jewish Congress (WJC) spokesman told Reuters Herzog was extremely concerned about both issues and sought just solutions.

The issue of compensation for Jewish Holocaust survivors in eastern Europe gained attention in January when the opposition Greens launched a draft law to ensure those in the East receive the same benefits as their counterparts in the West.

Germany has paid about 100 billion marks (almost $60 billion) in compensation since the war for victims of Nazi injustice, but those in the East received one-off payments to a maximum of 1,000 marks while those living in Germany get about 500 marks a month.

The explosive issue of pension payments to war criminals surfaced in December, when the WJC called on Germany to publish the names of former members of Hitler's Waffen SS veterans who live in Britain and the United States and receive disability pensions.

The German government refused, saying strict data protection laws prevented it from releasing such a list of names. It said, however, that any application for a pension was checked with Nazi-hunting centres and archives in Germany.
Rexrodt said the confidentiality questions revolving around the issue of pension payments had to be resolved.
Meanwhile, the German Central Council of Jews said they had talked to Rexrodt about the integration of Jewish immigrants from the former Societ Union into the existing German Jewish community.
Leaders of the European Jewish Congress discussed the harmonisation of laws against xenophobia, racism and anti-Semitism across Europe. ($ = 1.707 German Marks)
